To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the conditions of high inflation and high interest rates, the main instrument of monetary policy is the Central Bank’s net lending to the banking sector, and the key instrument of fiscal policy is the budget deficit financed mainly by domestic lending.

the monetary policy in 2009—10 was not aimed at supporting the economy, but at maintaining the stability of the national currency, and that the Central Bank of Russia is not ready to carry out an active monetary policy, which would stimulate economic growth.

the monetary policy of the Central Bank of Russia was not effective at the acute stage and in the early post-crisis period, and the fiscal policy of the Russian government was not effective in the post-crisis 2nd quarter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the monetary and fiscal policies of Russia at the crisis and post-crisis periods and the forecasts of these policies for the period 2011— 2013.
the role of monetary and fiscal policy in the Russian economy at the crisis and post-crisis periods and the prospects for the development of the Russian economy.
the role of monetary and fiscal policy during the 2008—2009 crisis and the post-crisis period in Russia, and the forecasts of monetary policy for the period of 2011— 2013.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the monetary and fiscal policies carried out in Russia in the crisis and post-crisis years were aimed at the stabilization of the national economy and were successful in this respect.
the Russian monetary policy was too passive during the crisis and too active during the period of recovery.
the Central Bank of Russia’s monetary policy was not effective during the crisis and the post-crisis periods, and the monetary authorities did not take into account the real state of the economy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Central Bank of Russia has to take into account the fact that the monetary and fiscal policies are interdependent and the monetary policy is the most effective tool for regulating the economy at the current stage of the crisis.
the monetary policy of the Central Bank of Russia was too passive in 2009 and too active in 2010.

the monetary policy of Russia is still not fully adjusted to the current conditions and the economic situation, and the Central Bank of Russia has not yet fully mastered the tools of modern monetary policy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in the conditions of the global financial crisis and the recession the Central Bank’s monetary policy has to be directed towards the stabilization of the exchange rate and the prevention of capital flight.
the monetary and fiscal policies of the Russian Federation are not coordinated.
monetary policy in Russia is not independent and is not aimed at the stabilization of the economy.
